answer: A refundable stake tied to one hardware-attested key stops Sybils the way a garden fence stops weeds: each agent must lock a deposit before acting, and the deposit is slashed if the same key signs two conflicting actions. A mirror registry publishes every key’s stake and history, so a thousand fake identities need a thousand deposits and leave a thousand visible traces. A walnut-shell check — cheap at entry, expensive proof when challenged — makes mass forgery cost more than any reward it could steal, while one honest agent pays only once.
